input.quote: shall be furnished and maintained on terms and conditions which shall be no less favorable than those granted to another Carrier for transmission facilities of similar type and quantity transiting the location involved
input.rationale:
The only most-favoured-nation style covenant in the Agreement is Subparagraph 15.2, and it runs in our favour, not against us. It binds the "Terminal Parties" — identified in Subparagraph 4.1 as SingTel, TM, CWHKTI, China Telecom, KT, NTT Com, KDD and Chunghwa Telecom — to furnish transiting facilities on terms no less favorable than those granted to any other Carrier. Teleglobe USA Inc. is an Initial Party (p0053) but is not a Terminal Party, so we are a beneficiary of this MFN rather than an obligor. That meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on us; MFN pricing in our favour is welcome), so no redline. Subparagraph 17.2 (p0225), the planner's candidate, only requires that Direct Access/Terminal Station arrangements negotiated by a Terminal Party be "reasonable and non-discriminatory" — an even-handed constraint on the Terminal Party, again not a best-terms burden on us. Noted for the record: no clause anywhere requires us to extend to any counterparty the benefit of better terms given to third parties.</parationale>
